sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for Dealbook, a daily newsletter at the
sentences.zh: 我负责《纽约时报》每日简讯Dealbook的商业与政策报道。

sentences.en: New York Times.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市Dealbook峰会的现场，采访商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的领袖，其中包括J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜

sentences.en: Lagarde, Zylran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the Dealbook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及许多其他人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以实时观看其中一些毫无防备、未经过滤的对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at nytimes.com on November
sentences.zh: 我们将于11月18日在nytimes.com上直播部分采访，供任何人免费观看。

sentences.en: 18th.
If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅者，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并获得一个月免费访问我们所有新闻报道的权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 我希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这里是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today.
sentences.zh: 今天。

sentences.en: In the coming days, lawmakers in France are poised to adopt controversial legislation to combat the
sentences.zh: 在接下来的几天里，法国议员准备通过一项备受争议的立法，以打击

sentences.en: threat of Islamist radicals, which the country's president has called, quote, the enemy of the republic.
sentences.zh: 伊斯兰激进分子的威胁，法国总统称其为“共和国的敌人”。

sentences.en: My colleague, Constant Meir, on the debate raging there about the role of government in religion.
sentences.zh: 我的同事康斯坦·迈尔将探讨法国国内围绕政府在宗教中扮演的角色展开的激烈辩论。

sentences.en: It's Friday, February 12th.
sentences.zh: 今天是2月12日，星期五。

sentences.en: Constant, tell me about Samuel Paddy.
sentences.zh: 康斯坦，跟我聊聊塞缪尔·帕蒂吧。

sentences.en: Samuel Paddy was a history and civics teacher in a suburb north of Paris called Conflans-Saint-Honorine.
sentences.zh: 塞缪尔·帕蒂是巴黎北部一个叫孔夫兰-圣奥诺里纳的郊区的一名历史和公民课老师。

sentences.en: He was 47 years old.
sentences.zh: 他47岁。

sentences.en: He had been teaching for more than 20 years.
sentences.zh: 他教书已经超过20年了。

sentences.en: And almost all of Paddy's former students I talked to told me that he was that type of teacher who was always eager to stimulate their
sentences.zh: 几乎所有我采访过的帕蒂的前学生都告诉我，他是那种总是渴望激发他们

sentences.en: critical thinking, always eager to organize debates.
sentences.zh: 批判性思维、总是热衷于组织辩论的老师。

sentences.en: Sounds like he was a good teacher.
sentences.zh: 听起来他是个好老师。

sentences.en: He was a great teacher.
sentences.zh: 他是个伟大的老师。

sentences.en: I mean, he was really beloved by his students.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他真的很受学生爱戴。

sentences.en: And he was always this teacher who, again, according to students I talked to, who basically left his mark.
sentences.zh: 而且根据我采访的学生的说法，他一直是一位能给人留下深刻印记的老师。

sentences.en: So last October, he goes to class to give his lesson on freedom of expression, which is a lesson he'd given years and years before.
sentences.zh: 所以去年10月，他去上关于言论自由的课，这门课他几年前就讲过。

sentences.en: And it's actually part of the French national curriculum.
sentences.zh: 这其实是法国国家课程的一部分。

sentences.en: And the way he normally taught this lesson was by challenging students to engage with what could be considered offensive.
sentences.zh: 他通常上这门课的方式是挑战学生去接触那些可能被认为具有攻击性的内容。

sentences.en: And he did that by showing two caricatures of the Prophet Muhammad, including one where Prophet Muhammad is naked.
sentences.zh: 他是通过展示两幅先知穆罕默德的漫画来做到这一点的，其中包括一幅先知穆罕默德赤身裸体的漫画。

sentences.en: And here, you need to understand something about France in general.
sentences.zh: 在这里，你需要了解一些关于法国总体情况的事。

sentences.en: Over the years, the Muslim population has grown substantially.
sentences.zh: 这些年来，穆斯林人口大幅增长。

sentences.en: And today, it's one of the biggest minorities in Western Europe.
sentences.zh: 如今，它是西欧最大的少数群体之一。

sentences.en: And this was also the case for this town, Conflans-Saint-Honorine.
sentences.zh: 孔夫兰-圣奥诺里纳这个小镇也是如此。

sentences.en: And so, taking that into consideration, Paddy told students that if they found the cartoons offensive, they could leave the classroom or look away.
sentences.zh: 因此，考虑到这一点，帕蒂告诉学生，如果他们觉得这些漫画具有攻击性，可以离开教室或把目光移开。

sentences.en: And he considered this kind of a nice gesture.
sentences.zh: 他认为这算是一种友好的姿态。

sentences.en: But this gesture was actually seen by several parents as discriminatory, as a way to single out Muslim students.
sentences.zh: 但这个姿态在几位家长看来实际上具有歧视性，是孤立穆斯林学生的一种方式。

sentences.en: And so, you have some Muslim parents starting to complain to the school director.
sentences.zh: 于是，一些穆斯林家长开始向学校校长投诉。

sentences.en: And after a few days of internal tensions at the school, and after everybody understood that Samuel Paty had actually only been a bit
sentences.zh: 在学校内部经历了几天紧张气氛，且大家都明白塞缪尔·帕蒂要求学生离开教室其实只是有点

sentences.en: clumsy, perhaps, when he asked students to leave the classroom, well, he apologized.
sentences.zh: 笨拙之后，嗯，他道歉了。

sentences.en: And everything seemed to be back to normal, you know, at least in the school.
sentences.zh: 一切似乎都回到了正常状态，你知道的，至少在学校里是这样。

sentences.en: So this felt like a kind of run-of-the-mill case of a teacher offering a provocative lesson about freedom
sentences.zh: 所以这感觉就像是一个普通的案例，一个老师上了一堂关于言论自由的挑衅性课程

sentences.en: of speech, and there being a small controversy in the school, but he apologized, and everything seemed to be okay.
sentences.zh: ，学校里也起了一点小争议，但他道歉了，一切似乎都安然无恙。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But...
sentences.zh: 但是……

sentences.en: On the internet, one angry father complained about the teacher in videos.
sentences.zh: 在互联网上，一位愤怒的父亲在视频中抱怨这位老师。

sentences.en: For example, he said that his daughter was asked to leave the classroom because she was Muslim, which was not the case.
sentences.zh: 例如，他说他的女儿被要求离开教室，因为她是穆斯林，但事实并非如此。

sentences.en: In fact, she was never in the class.
sentences.zh: 事实上，她根本没在那节课上。

sentences.en: And Samuel Paty did not ask Muslim students to leave, he offered it as an option.
sentences.zh: 塞缪尔·帕蒂并没有要求穆斯林学生离开，他只是把它作为一种选择提供出来。

sentences.en: And so, this father starts to describe what happened in a twisted way, saying that this teacher was acting in a hateful way.
sentences.zh: 于是，这位父亲开始以扭曲的方式描述发生的事情，称这位老师行为充满仇恨。

sentences.en: And he caused people to pressure the school to expel the teacher.
sentences.zh: 他煽动人们向学校施压，要求开除这名老师。

sentences.en: Huh.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So the video goes viral on social media, and it reaches a guy named Adulak Anzorov.
sentences.zh: 所以这段视频在社交媒体上广为流传，并传到了一个叫阿杜拉克·安佐罗夫的人那里。

sentences.en: Anzorov is 18 years old.
sentences.zh: 安佐罗夫18岁。

sentences.en: He was born in Russia, he's Chechen, he's Muslim.
sentences.zh: 他出生在俄罗斯，是车臣人，也是穆斯林。

sentences.en: He came to France when he was six years old, and he was raised in the French public school system.
sentences.zh: 他六岁时来到法国，在法国公立学校体系中长大。

sentences.en: He was very much a product of this system.
sentences.zh: 他可以说是这个体系的产物。

sentences.en: And then last year, he started to become radicalized on the internet.
sentences.zh: 然后去年，他开始在互联网上被极端化。

sentences.en: He was adhering to a vision of Islam that was very extremiSt.
sentences.zh: 他信奉一种非常极端的伊斯兰教愿景。

sentences.en: And so, he sees what happened in Conflans-en-Tonorine, and he decides to go there.
sentences.zh: 因此，他看到了发生在孔夫兰-圣奥诺里纳的事，并决定去那里。

sentences.en: And he comes to the school where Paty teaches, and he waits for him.
sentences.zh: 他来到了帕蒂教书的学校，并在那里等他。

sentences.en: And soon enough, Paty leaves the school to go home, and then Anzorov follows him down the street.
sentences.zh: 没过多久，帕蒂离开学校回家，安佐罗夫便在街上跟踪他。

sentences.en: And after a few hundred meters, he comes after him, and he stabs him, and he beheads him with a big knife.
sentences.zh: 走了几百米后，他追了上去，刺伤了他，并用一把大刀将他斩首。

sentences.en: Oh, that's awful.
sentences.zh: 哦，太可怕了。

sentences.en: That's horrific.
sentences.zh: 这太骇人听闻了。

sentences.en: And after he beheads him, he takes a photo, he publishes it online, on Twitter, and he has a message that is addressed to President Emmanuel Macron of France.
sentences.zh: 在他将他斩首后，他拍了一张照片，将其发布到推特等网络上，并附上了一条针对法国总统埃马纽埃尔·马克龙的信息。

sentences.en: And the message reads,
sentences.zh: 信息写道：

sentences.en: In the name of Allah, the most gracious, the most merciful, from Abdullah, the servant of Allah, to Macron, the leader of the infidels,
sentences.zh: 奉至仁至慈的真主之名，从真主的仆人阿卜杜拉，到异教徒的头目马克龙，

sentences.en: I executed one of your hell dogs, who dared to belittle Muhammad.
sentences.zh: 我处决了你们的一条地狱恶犬，他胆敢贬低穆罕默德。

sentences.en: Call misfellows before you are inflicted a harsh punishment.
sentences.zh: 在你们遭受严厉惩罚之前，管好你们这群同类。

sentences.en: So, this is clearly an act of terrorism, in every way.
sentences.zh: 所以，这在各方面显然都是恐怖主义行为。

sentences.en: It is, in every way.
sentences.zh: 在各方面都是。

sentences.en: And after a few minutes, he is spotted in the street by the police officers, and they kill him.
sentences.zh: 几分钟后，他在街上被警察发现，并被当场击毙。

sentences.en: What is the reaction in France to what happened to Samuel Paddy?
sentences.zh: 法国对塞缪尔·帕蒂遭遇的不幸有什么反应？

sentences.en: People are outraged.
sentences.zh: 人们感到愤怒。

sentences.en: People are mourning, because it feels that this attack could have struck at their own friends, at their own teachers.
sentences.zh: 人们在哀悼，因为他们觉得这场袭击可能就降临在他们自己的朋友、他们自己的老师身上。

sentences.en: And you have to remember that, you know, this attack comes on the heels of a string of very deadly attacks that started in 2015.
sentences.zh: 你必须记住，你知道的，这次袭击紧接着自2015年开始的一连串极其致命的袭击。

sentences.en: Now, returning to our breaking news story, we are getting reports of a shooting at the French satirical magazine,
sentences.zh: 现在，回到我们的突发新闻报道，我们收到报道称法国讽刺杂志

sentences.en: Charlie Hebdo, in Paris.
sentences.zh: 《查理周刊》位于巴黎的办公室发生枪击事件。

sentences.en: First was the January 2015 attack against the Charlie Hebdo journalists that left about a dozen people dead.
sentences.zh: 首先是2015年1月针对《查理周刊》记者的袭击，导致大约十几人丧生。

sentences.en: Bloodbath engulfed Paris tonight as terror attacks exploded across the French capital.
sentences.zh: 今晚血洗巴黎，恐怖袭击在法国首都各地爆发。

sentences.en: At least six sites were hit.
sentences.zh: 至少有六个地点遭到袭击。

sentences.en: Tonight, one at the Stade de France.
sentences.zh: 今晚，一处在法兰西体育场。

sentences.en: From a concert hall.
sentences.zh: 从一个音乐厅。

sentences.en: Two more attacks.
sentences.zh: 还有另外两起袭击。

sentences.en: To a shopping mall.
sentences.zh: 到一个购物中心。

sentences.en: Gunmen with Kalashnikovs reported.
sentences.zh: 据报道有手持卡拉什尼科夫冲锋枪的枪手。

sentences.en: To a restaurant.
sentences.zh: 到一家餐馆。

sentences.en: And then you had the attack in November 2015 around the Bataclan and in and around Paris, striking at cafes, restaurants.
sentences.zh: 然后是2015年11月发生在巴塔克兰剧院以及巴黎市内及周边的袭击，打击了咖啡馆和餐馆。

sentences.en: And that left more than a hundred people dead.
sentences.zh: 那场袭击导致一百多人丧生。

sentences.en: An evening of national celebration turned into a scene of horror when a truck plowed into a crowd in southern France.
sentences.zh: 当一辆卡车冲入法国南部的人群时，一个全国欢庆的夜晚变成了一场恐怖的场景。

sentences.en: And then over the next couple of years, you had an attack in Nice with someone driving a truck over a very busy street, leaving more than 50 or so people dead.
sentences.zh: 在接下来的几年里，尼斯发生了一起袭击事件，有人驾驶卡车碾压一条非常繁忙的街道，造成50多人死亡。

sentences.en: With breaking news from France, where a few hours ago, a gunman opened fire on a Christmas market in Strasbourg, or killing at least two people.
sentences.zh: 关于法国的突发新闻，几个小时前，一名枪手在斯特拉斯堡的圣诞市场上开枪，造成至少两人死亡。

sentences.en: And then a string of very specific attacks that felt like France was constantly under this threat of terror attacks.
sentences.zh: 接着是一连串非常具体的袭击，让人感觉法国时刻处于恐怖袭击的威胁之下。

sentences.en: But meanwhile, France is grieving.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，法国在悲痛。

sentences.en: And not just for the dead.
sentences.zh: 不仅是为了死者。

sentences.en: The French are also in grief because they know their country will struggle to recover from these wounds.
sentences.zh: 法国人也在悲痛，因为他们知道自己的国家将难以从这些伤口中恢复过来。

sentences.en: And they fear what will come next.
sentences.zh: 他们害怕接下来会发生什么。

sentences.en: But in 2019, and in the beginning of 2020, those attacks started to stop, you know.
sentences.zh: 但在2019年和2020年初，这些袭击开始停止了。

sentences.en: And so this fear started to decrease until the killing of Samuel Petit.
sentences.zh: 所以这种恐惧开始减少，直到塞缪尔·帕蒂遇害。

sentences.en: And so the killing not only revives old wounds of terrorism in France, but it also points to a threat that is changing, that is becoming increasingly homegrown.
sentences.zh: 因此，这起谋杀不仅重燃了法国国内恐怖主义的旧伤，也指向了一种正在改变、正日益本土化的威胁。

sentences.en: And that actually changes the issue because you're dealing with people who are self-radicalized,
sentences.zh: 这实际上改变了问题，因为你面对的是自我激进化的人，

sentences.en: who are unknown to the intelligence services, who have no clear links to terrorist groups.
sentences.zh: 他们不为情报部门所知，与恐怖组织没有清晰的联系。

sentences.en: And so it indirectly calls into question the way we respond to those attacks.
sentences.zh: 因此，它间接让人质疑我们应对这些袭击的方式。

sentences.en: For years, French authorities had been pushing ahead on various anti-terrorism measures.
sentences.zh: 多年来，法国当局一直在推进各项反恐措施。

sentences.en: But now they're looking at other solutions, other options.
sentences.zh: 但现在他们正在寻找其他解决方案、其他选项。

sentences.en: They want to go deeper.
sentences.zh: 他们想要更深入。

sentences.en: They want to get to the root of the issue.
sentences.zh: 他们想要触及问题的根源。

sentences.en: And this is the moment when the debate lands at a bedrock of French society, at a concept that is really deep inside our national psyche, which is called laïcité.
sentences.zh: 正是在这个时候，辩论触及了法国社会的基石，触及了我们国家心灵深处的一个概念，即所谓的“世俗主义”（laïcité）。

sentences.en: And what is laïcité?
sentences.zh: 什么是“世俗主义”？

sentences.en: Am I saying it correctly?
sentences.zh: 我发音正确吗？

sentences.en: Laïcité.
sentences.zh: 世俗主义。

sentences.en: Laïcité, yeah.
sentences.zh: 世俗主义，对。

sentences.en: Let's find this way.
sentences.zh: 我们这样理解。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So laïcité is a principle.
sentences.zh: 所以世俗主义是一个原则。

sentences.en: And if we wanted to simplify things, I would say that it's about the separation between the state and the church.
sentences.zh: 如果我们想把事情简单化，我会说它关乎国家与教会的分离。

sentences.en: So this is something that is familiar for Americans.
sentences.zh: 所以这对美国人来说是熟悉的概念。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Something that we could actually translate by secularism.
sentences.zh: 我们可以把它翻译为“世俗主义”（secularism）。

sentences.en: But in France, it has some sort of a bigger meaning.
sentences.zh: 但在法国，它有着某种更宏大的意义。

sentences.en: In France, this idea behind laïcité is that it's about freedom from religion.
sentences.zh: 在法国，世俗主义背后的这个理念是摆脱宗教的自由。

sentences.en: You know, whereas in the U.S., it's really about freedom of religion.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，而在美国，它实际上是宗教自由。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And freedom from the government impinging on religion.
sentences.zh: 以及免受政府干涉宗教的自由。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: You know, in France, there's this idea that it's all about preventing religion from impinging into state affairs.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，在法国，有一种观点认为，这一切都是为了防止宗教干涉国家事务。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So that's fascinating in theory.
sentences.zh: 所以这在理论上非常迷人。

sentences.en: How does this principle of laïcité actually get applied in France?
sentences.zh: 这个世俗主义原则在法国实际上是如何应用的呢？

sentences.en: I know that, Constant, you grew up in France.
sentences.zh: 我知道，康斯坦，你在法国长大。

sentences.en: So I'm guessing you have seen it firsthand.
sentences.zh: 所以我猜你亲眼见证过。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Probably the best place to explain this concept is the school, which are considered a public space.
sentences.zh: 解释这个概念最好的地方可能是学校，学校被视为公共空间。

sentences.en: There is this idea in laïcité that students are not allowed to wear ostentatious religious signs in school because it is a public space.
sentences.zh: 世俗主义中有一种观点认为，学生不允许在学校佩戴外露的宗教标志，因为这是一个公共空间。

sentences.en: It is a neutral space.
sentences.zh: 这是一个中立的空间。

sentences.en: So when I was in middle school, I think that was grade eight, and there was a fellow classmate, you know, at some point in a class.
sentences.zh: 所以当我上初中时，我想那是八年级，有一次在课堂上，有一位同学。

sentences.en: He was wearing this cross around his neck.
sentences.zh: 他脖子上戴着一个十字架。

sentences.en: And our math teacher, if I remember well, you know, just asked him just to hide that cross just under his t-shirt, right?
sentences.zh: 如果我没记错的话，我们的数学老师只是让他把那个十字架藏在T恤里面，对吧？

sentences.en: Which is kind of surprising.
sentences.zh: 这有点令人惊讶。

sentences.en: But I mean, my classmate agreed.
sentences.zh: 但我的同学同意了。

sentences.en: And that was completely fine, actually quite natural, because again, there was this atmosphere that laïcité has to be implemented in the public space.
sentences.zh: 而且这完全没问题，实际上相当自然，因为同样地，当时有一种必须在公共空间落实世俗主义的氛围。

sentences.en: And what else than a better public space than school?
sentences.zh: 还有什么比学校更好的公共空间呢？

sentences.en: Okay, so what is the history behind this concept?
sentences.zh: 好吧，那么这个概念背后的历史是什么？

sentences.en: Where exactly does it come from?
sentences.zh: 它究竟源于何处？

sentences.en: You have to go back to the French Revolution, 1789.
sentences.zh: 你必须追溯到1789年的法国大革命。

sentences.en: For centuries, the Catholic Church was incredibly powerful financially, politically, up until the late 1700s.
sentences.zh: 几个世纪以来，天主教会拥有极其强大的财政和政治权力，一直持续到18世纪末。

sentences.en: And that's when the French Revolution happened.
sentences.zh: 也就是在那时，法国大革命爆发了。

sentences.en: And it largely put an end to the reign of the Catholic Church in France.
sentences.zh: 这场革命在很大程度上终结了天主教会对法国的统治。

sentences.en: And for the next century, for the 19th century, it's pretty much a constant battle between the
sentences.zh: 在随后的一个世纪，即19世纪，这几乎成了一场持续不断的博弈，双方是

sentences.en: church and the state, you know, with this idea that the Catholic Church should not get too much power.
sentences.zh: 教会与国家，你知道的，当时的共识是天主教会不应掌握过大的权力。

sentences.en: This battle is, you know, sometimes quite violent.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这种博弈有时相当激烈。

sentences.en: And it leads to this 1905 law, which was really the first one that rooted into legal terms, this
sentences.zh: 它最终促成了1905年的一项法律，这也是真正从法律层面上确立

sentences.en: principle of laïcité, making sure that religions should not interfere in state affairs, meaning that you are allowed to practice a religion privately.
sentences.zh: 政教分离原则的第一部法律，确保宗教不得干预国家事务，这意味着允许个人私下信仰宗教。

sentences.en: But it should not be, you know, this kind of constant presence in the public life.
sentences.zh: 但这不应该成为公众生活中那种无处不在、持续存在的现象。

sentences.en: And at the same time, it is expected that the state does not interfere in religious affairs.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，国家也被期望不干预宗教事务。

sentences.en: The state is not there to support any religion, nor to repress any religion.
sentences.zh: 国家既不应该支持任何宗教，也不应该压制任何宗教。

sentences.en: So the element of this concept and this 1905 law that feels most distinct, especially to my American ears, is this freedom from religion.
sentences.zh: 因此，这个概念和1905年这部法律中让我觉得最独特的部分——尤其是站在我这个美国人的角度——就是这种免于宗教干预的自由。

sentences.en: And you're saying that comes from this long history of France trying to be free from the power of the Catholic Church.
sentences.zh: 你的意思是，这源于法国长期以来试图摆脱天主教会权力的历史。

sentences.en: And therefore, this concept and this law, it attempts to address this deep suspicion of a religion's influence on the state.
sentences.zh: 因此，这个概念和这部法律试图解决的，正是对宗教影响力干涉国家事务的深深戒备。

sentences.en: Right, exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错，确实如此。

sentences.en: And so how does this principle of laïcité evolve over time?
sentences.zh: 那么，政教分离原则是随着时间如何演变的呢？

sentences.en: Laïcité was largely untouched for most of the 20th century.
sentences.zh: 在整个20世纪的大部分时间里，政教分离原则基本上没有受到触动。

sentences.en: And that could be because France at the time was largely homogenous.
sentences.zh: 这可能是因为当时的法国在很大程度上是一个单一文化国家。

sentences.en: But that starts to change with an influx of immigrants from Muslim countries.
sentences.zh: 但随着大量来自穆斯林国家的移民涌入，这种情况开始发生变化。

sentences.en: And that leads to the law being first really tested in the 80s and the 90s.
sentences.zh: 这也导致这项法律在80年代和90年代首次真正经受考验。

sentences.en: In 1989, you had three girls, three young girls in a middle school who refused to take off their headscarves.
sentences.zh: 在1989年，有三个女孩，三名初中女生拒绝摘下她们的头巾。

sentences.en: And because of that, they were expelled by their director.
sentences.zh: 正因如此，她们被校长开除了。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And, you know, at the time, it was kind of a small controversy, at least when it started.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，在当时这只是一场小风波，至少在刚开始的时候是这样。

sentences.en: But then it really sparks off a whole debate on the wearing of the veil in schools.
sentences.zh: 但随后它真正引发了关于在学校佩戴面纱的全民大辩论。

sentences.en: And there is this decision, this judgment by Francis Supreme Court a few months later that say that
sentences.zh: 几个月后，法国最高法院作出了一项裁决，称

sentences.en: wearing headscarves in schools is actually not incompatible with the principle of laïcité.
sentences.zh: 在学校佩戴头巾其实并不与政教分离原则相抵触。

sentences.en: Not incompatible, so it's allowed.
sentences.zh: 不相抵触，也就是说这是允许的。

sentences.en: Not incompatible, right.
sentences.zh: 不相抵触，没错。

sentences.en: But the debate had taken root in the country.
sentences.zh: 但这场辩论已经在国内扎下了根。

sentences.en: And so in the following years, you have new incidents in schools that are reported, especially
sentences.zh: 所以在接下来的几年里，学校里开始出现新的事件并被报道，特别是

sentences.en: in the French press, of young guys who are pressuring young girls to wear a headscarf in school.
sentences.zh: 在法国媒体上，报道了一些年轻男孩向女同学施压，迫使她们在学校佩戴头巾的情况。

sentences.en: And that started to kind of worry people.
sentences.zh: 这开始让人们感到有些担忧。

sentences.en: And so the government responds to that new challenge by passing a law in 2004 that bans the wearing of religious signs, of ostentatious religious signs in schools.
sentences.zh: 因此，政府通过在2004年颁布一项法律来应对这一新挑战，该法律禁止在学校佩戴宗教标志，即显眼的宗教标志。

sentences.en: And I'm going to guess, based on my understanding of your age, that when you were in school and
sentences.zh: 我想根据我对你年龄的了解来猜一下，当你还在上学时，

sentences.en: your classmate was asked to hide his cross, that that law would have been in practice.
sentences.zh: 当你的同班同学被要求把十字架藏起来时，那项法律应该已经开始实施了。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Okay, so at this point in the history of laïcité, it feels like France is having to make a choice, right?
sentences.zh: 好的，所以在政教分离历史的这个阶段，感觉法国似乎不得不做出选择，对吗？

sentences.en: Do we as a country adjust the way we view this concept of the separation of church and state to accommodate the religious practices of new arrivals, especially Muslims?
sentences.zh: 我们作为一个国家，是否应该调整我们对政教分离这一概念的看法，以适应新移民特别是穆斯林的宗教习俗？

sentences.en: Or do we force people to change their practices?
sentences.zh: 还是说我们应该强迫人们改变他们的习俗？

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And the choice that France makes at the time is to force people to accommodate with the
sentences.zh: 而法国当时做出的选择，是强迫人们去适应

sentences.en: French model of integration.
sentences.zh: 法国的融合模式。

sentences.en: And I just mentioned the 2004 law.
sentences.zh: 我刚才提到了2004年的法律。

sentences.en: There is actually a second law that was passed in 2010.
sentences.zh: 实际上，在2010年还通过了第二项法律。

sentences.en: And this time, it banned the full-face veil in streets, in public spaces, in basically public
sentences.zh: 这一次，它禁止在街道、公共场所、基本上所有的公共

sentences.en: buildings, with this idea that the full-face veil actually breaks with this principle of equality
sentences.zh: 建筑中穿戴全脸面纱，其背后的理念是，全脸面纱实际上打破了男女平等的原则，

sentences.en: between women and men because it is some sort of a subjugation of women, you know, to men.
sentences.zh: 因为它某种程度上是对女性的一种压制，你知道的，是男性对女性的压迫。

sentences.en: So laïcité is once again codified into French law, and if we're being candid, in a way that targets Muslim religious practices.
sentences.zh: 因此，政教分离再次被写入法国法律，坦白来讲，这种方式的目标正是穆斯林的宗教习俗。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, again, the 2004 law, the 2010 law, it's all about banning religious signs.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，重申一下，2004年的法律，2010年的法律，核心全都是关于禁止宗教标志。

sentences.en: But true, we need to be honest there.
sentences.zh: 但说实话，我们必须对此诚实。

sentences.en: The real aim, you know, is targeting Muslim practices.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，真正的目标正是针对穆斯林的习俗。

sentences.en: I have to imagine that as this is happening and these laws are accumulating, for some Muslim
sentences.zh: 我禁不住想象，随着这一切的发生，这些法律不断累积，对于法国的一些穆斯林

sentences.en: people in France, this is starting to feel kind of repressive and maybe even a bit discriminatory.
sentences.zh: 群体来说，这开始让他们感到一种压迫感，甚至可能带有一点歧视色彩。

sentences.en: And asking them to give up a pretty big part of their identity.
sentences.zh: 并且要求他们放弃自己身份认同中相当重要的一部分。

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And this is a debate that we have had for the past two decades, basically, trying to make sense of laïcité, whether it is something that actually helps people to integrate into
sentences.zh: 这是我们过去二十年里一直在进行的一场辩论，基本上是在试图理解政教分离的真正意义，它究竟是真正能帮助人们融入

sentences.en: society or whether it is a tool that oppresses more and more people, and especially Muslim people.
sentences.zh: 社会的工具，还是一个越来越压迫更多人、特别是压迫穆斯林群体的工具。

sentences.en: It's actually a debate about the model of integration in France, really.
sentences.zh: 这其实是一场关于法国融合模式的辩论。

sentences.en: Do you assimilate, meaning that you need to change your own practices so that you resemble people?
sentences.zh: 你是选择同化，这意味着你需要改变自己的习俗，以便让自己看上去和大家一样？

sentences.en: Or do you integrate in a way that allows you to keep your traditions, your behaviors, and that doesn't prompt the backlash from the rest of the society?
sentences.zh: 还是选择一种能够让你保留自己的传统、行为方式，同时又不会引起社会其他部分强烈反弹的融合方式？

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用程序？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 解锁版？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 众所周知，你需要订阅《时报》才能阅读所有的报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果你可以免费体验《时报》一个月，且无需绑定信用卡呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你首次下载《纽约时报》应用时，你在该应用中的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 有一个月的时间去探索付费墙背后的内容，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载《时报》应用，即可获得30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: So, Constant, how does the murder, the horrific killing of Samuel Pate influence this decades-long debate about laïcité?
sentences.zh: 那么，孔斯唐（Constant），萨缪尔·帕蒂（Samuel Pate）遇害这一骇人听闻的谋杀案，是如何影响这场长达数十年的关于政教分离的辩论的呢？

sentences.en: So, President Emmanuel Macron had been working on a package of laws to deal with the growing threat of Muslim radicalism for several months.
sentences.zh: 所以，法兰西共和国总统埃马纽埃尔·马克龙（Emmanuel Macron）几个月来一直在致力于制定一揽子法律，以应对日益严重的穆斯林激进主义威胁。

sentences.en: We need to remember that it's been five years that France has been regularly the target of terrible terrorism attacks.
sentences.zh: 我们需要记住，五年来法国一直是恐怖主义袭击的频繁目标。

sentences.en: So, this attack on Samuel Pate really comes on the heels of years of terror attacks in
sentences.zh: 因此，针对萨缪尔·帕蒂的这次袭击，确实发生在法国多年恐怖袭击的紧要关头。

sentences.en: France.
sentences.zh: 法国。

sentences.en: And so, this attack really creates an incentive for the government to dabble down on laïcité
sentences.zh: 所以，这次袭击确实为政府提供了动力，使其在政教分离问题上采取更强硬立场，

sentences.en: and to use laïcité as a tool to respond to this growing threat of Muslim radicalism in the country.
sentences.zh: 并将政教分离作为一种工具，来应对国内日益严峻的穆斯林激进主义威胁。

sentences.en: And so, part of this package is about banning homeschooling for kids over three years old.
sentences.zh: 因此，这一揽子计划的一部分内容是禁止对三岁以上的儿童进行在家教育。

sentences.en: Because there's this fear that children who would be educated at home in an atmosphere that is a sort of
sentences.zh: 因为人们担心，在家中某种类似于

sentences.en: Islamist environment, it would be a threat for the republic.
sentences.zh: 伊斯兰主义环境的氛围里接受教育的儿童，将会对共和国构成威胁。

sentences.en: There is also a legislation that would curb online hate speech, the kind of hate speech that led to the killing of Samuel Pate.
sentences.zh: 其中还有一项旨在遏制网络仇恨言论的立法，正是这种仇恨言论导致了萨缪尔·帕蒂的遇害。

sentences.en: And there's also a provision that would rein in community associations, but also religious associations,
sentences.zh: 此外还有一项条款，旨在通过强制社区协会以及宗教协会

sentences.en: by obliging them to sign declaration of allegiance to so-called values of the republic.
sentences.zh: 签署效忠所谓共和国价值观的声明，来对其进行约束。

sentences.en: And it would also impose stricter controls on their fundings.
sentences.zh: 并且还将对它们的资金来源实施更严格的管控。

sentences.en: So, making religious groups sign a document that says we pledge essentially our loyalty to the state.
sentences.zh: 所以，就是让宗教团体签署一份文件，本质上表明我们承诺效忠国家。

sentences.en: Yes, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全正确。

sentences.en: And so, how are French Muslims responding to this overall package of laws?
sentences.zh: 那么，法国穆斯林对这一揽子整体法律有何反应？

sentences.en: Yeah, so, you have two reactions, I would say.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以，我想说大致有两种反应。

sentences.en: On the one hand, you have several imams or leading figures of Islam in France who support that bill,
sentences.zh: 一方面，法国的几位伊玛目或伊斯兰教领袖支持该法案，

sentences.en: saying that they have grown aware of their responsibility to make sure that a peaceful version of Islam is
sentences.zh: 他们表示，他们已经意识到自身的责任，即确保在清真寺中

sentences.en: promoted in mosques, and they're thinking that this bill will help them better control and restrict the way Islam is taught in France.
sentences.zh: 弘扬和平版本的伊斯兰教，他们认为该法案将有助于他们更好地控制和规范伊斯兰教在法国的传授方式。

sentences.en: On the other hand, you also have Muslims who feel that this law unfairly targets them and kind of conflates Islam with radical IslaMs.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，也有一些穆斯林感到这项法律不公平地针对他们，并且将伊斯兰教与激进伊斯兰教混为一谈。

sentences.en: And I think this is the thing they're really worried about, about this new atmosphere, about this new climate that, in a way, implies that religions can be, and especially Islam,
sentences.zh: 我认为这是他们真正担心的问题，关于这种新的氛围，关于这种在某种程度上暗示宗教（特别是伊斯兰教）

sentences.en: the starting point for separatism and extremism.
sentences.zh: 可以成为分裂主义和极端主义起点的全新舆论气候。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: So, it sounds like in their minds, this law maligns Islam.
sentences.zh: 听起来在他们看来，这项法律是在抹黑伊斯兰教。

sentences.en: It sees the religion itself as nurturing radicalism, and they don't agree with that.
sentences.zh: 它将宗教本身视为孕育激进主义的温床，而他们对此并不认同。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so, for Muslim people, it kind of creates this situation where you actually have an opposition
sentences.zh: 因此，对于穆斯林群体而言，这实际上造成了一种局面，即你的法兰西公民身份

sentences.en: between your French citizenship that does not allow you to express, you know, your religious beliefs, or at least that asks you not to express them too much,
sentences.zh: ——它不允许你表达你的宗教信仰，或者至少要求你不要过多表达——

sentences.en: and your religious identity that is seen as opposed, you know, to your French identity.
sentences.zh: 与你的宗教身份之间产生了对立，而你的宗教身份被视为与你的法国身份相冲突。

sentences.en: Rather than combining those two identities, this law risks dividing them even more.
sentences.zh: 这项法律非但没有将这两种身份结合起来，反而有进一步撕裂它们的风险。

sentences.en: Is anyone in France asking themselves whether, instead of trying to strengthen la cité, the country should be rethinking it, and rethinking it in the opposite direction?
sentences.zh: 法国是否有人在自问，与其努力强化政教分离，这个国家是否应该重新审视它，并且向相反的方向重新审视？

sentences.en: Which is to say, making religious immigrants feel welcomed and embraced for their religiousness.
sentences.zh: 也就是让宗教移民感受到他们的宗教信仰受到欢迎和接纳。

sentences.en: And is it possible that that might better serve the goal of assimilation and integration, and ultimately, making France safer?
sentences.zh: 有没有可能这会更好地服务于同化与融合的目标，并最终让法国变得更安全？

sentences.en: Well, it is a question that is very difficult to ask in France, because ultimately, that actually calls into question our very model of integration.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是一个在法国很难提出的问题，因为归根结底，这实际上是在对我们核心的融合模式提出质疑。

sentences.en: You know, France was based on this idea that to integrate people, you assimilate them, meaning that you try to have people looking quite similar, having the same culture,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，法国建立在这样一种理念之上：为了融合人们，你必须同化他们，这意味着你试图让人们看起来相当相似、拥有相同的文化、

sentences.en: having the same historical references, and, I mean, all in all, kind of behaving in a homogenous way.
sentences.zh: 拥有相同的历史参照，我的意思是，总而言之，以一种同质化的方式行事。

sentences.en: And laïste was part of that idea.
sentences.zh: 而政教分离正是这一理念的一部分。

sentences.en: But as the society in France grows diverse, as multiculturalism is increasing in France, well, this new reality kind of contradicts those ideas of assimilation.
sentences.zh: 但随着法国社会的日益多元化，随着法国多元文化主义的增长，这种新现实在某种程度上与同化理念相矛盾。

sentences.en: And so, if you try to think about a new model of laïcité, you actually have to think about a new model of integration.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你试图构思一个新的政教分离模式，你实际上就必须构思一个新的融合模式。

sentences.en: And the question of whether laïcité could fit into this new model of integration that accepts more diversity,
sentences.zh: 关于政教分离是否能够契合这种接纳更多多元化的融合新模式，

sentences.en: I'm not sure that it would work, you know, because it basically contradicts this very idea that we want everyone to be neutral about their religious beliefs and roots.
sentences.zh: 我不敢确信这是否行得通，你知道的，因为它从根本上与我们希望每个人对自己的宗教信仰和根源保持中立的理念相矛盾。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So you're saying France isn't quite ready to let go of this concept of assimilation.
sentences.zh: 所以你的意思是法国还没准备好放弃同化这个概念。

sentences.en: But I wonder if, over time, France is really going to have that choice, if it's really going to be in France's hands to make that decision.
sentences.zh: 但我想知道，随着时间的推移，法国真的还会有这种选择吗，这个决定是否真的还能掌握在法国自己手中？

sentences.en: Probably not.
sentences.zh: 可能不会。

sentences.en: Because at some point, and President Emmanuel Macron has acknowledged it himself,
sentences.zh: 因为在某种程度上，连埃马纽埃尔·马克龙总统本人也已经承认了这一点，

sentences.en: society is becoming more and more multicultural.
sentences.zh: 社会正在变得越来越多元文化。

sentences.en: And so you cannot remain in a model that worked well in the 1960s, but that does not fit with the reality in 2021.
sentences.zh: 因此，你无法继续停留在20世纪60年代行之有效、却不符合2021年现实的模式中。

sentences.en: But so far, and this law is a perfect example of that, it is true that France is kind of clinging on this perhaps ideal of assimilation.
sentences.zh: 但到目前为止，这项法律就是一个完美的例子，法国确实在某种程度上执着于这种或许理想化的同化政策。

sentences.en: But when are people going to question, you know, the very way they were raised and educated and the way they integrated immigrants,
sentences.zh: 但是，当人们开始反思他们从小接受的教育和培养方式，以及他们融合移民的方式时，

sentences.en: it's difficult to know when this is going to happen.
sentences.zh: 我们很难知道这一天究竟何时会到来。

sentences.en: Well, Constant, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 好的，孔斯唐，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: We appreciate your time.
sentences.zh: 感谢你抽出时间。

sentences.en: Thanks, Michael.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，迈克尔（Michael）。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.en: We humbly, humbly ask you to convict President Trump for the crime for which he is overwhelmingly guilty of.
sentences.zh: 我们谦卑地、卑微地恳请你们裁定特朗普总统犯有他难辞其咎的罪行。

sentences.en: On Thursday, the House Democrats prosecuting former President Trump concluded their case,
sentences.zh: 周四，负责弹劾前总统特朗普的众议院民主党人完成了他们的陈述，

sentences.en: branding him a danger to American democracy, who risks inciting new violence unless he is convicted and barred from holding office.
sentences.zh: 将他定性为美国民主的威胁，如果不将其定罪并剥夺其担任公职的资格，他将有可能煽动新的暴力。

sentences.en: Because if you don't, if we pretend this didn't happen, or worse, if we let it go unanswered,
sentences.zh: 因为如果不这样做，如果我们假装这一切没有发生，或者更糟糕的是，如果我们对此置之不理，

sentences.en: who's to say it won't happen again?
sentences.zh: 谁能保证这种事不会再次发生？

sentences.en: The impeachment managers, led by Congressman Jamie Raskin, appealed to senators from both parties to rise above partisanship and hold Trump accountable
sentences.zh: 由众议员杰米·拉斯金（Jamie Raskin）领导的弹劾经理团队呼吁两党参议员超越党派之争，让特朗普为他在国会大厦骚乱中所扮演的角色

sentences.en: for his role in the insurrection at the Capitol.
sentences.zh: 承担责任。

sentences.en: Senators, America, we need to exercise our common sense about what happened.
sentences.zh: 参议员们，全美同胞们，我们需要对所发生的事情运用我们的常识。

sentences.en: Let's not get caught up in a lot of outlandish lawyers' theories here.
sentences.zh: 让我们不要在这里陷入一大堆光怪陆离的律师理论中。

sentences.en: exercise your common sense about what just took place in our country.
sentences.zh: 请对我们国家刚刚发生的事情运用你们的常识。

sentences.en: Trump's defense lawyers will begin making their case for his acquittal later this morning.
sentences.zh: 特朗普的辩护律师将于今天上午晚些时候开始为他的无罪开辩。

sentences.en: And If you look at the projection, I would imagine by the time we get to April, that will be what I would call for, you know, for better wording, open season,
sentences.zh: 如果你看一下预测，我想象等我们到了四月份，那就会变成我称之为——换个更好的说法——全面开放的时期，

sentences.en: namely virtually everybody and anybody in any category could start to get vaccinated.
sentences.zh: 也就是基本上各个类别中的每一个普通人都可以开始接种疫苗。

sentences.en: In an interview with NBC News on Thursday,
sentences.zh: 在周四接受美国全国广播公司新闻（NBC News）采访时，

sentences.en: Dr. Anthony Fauci,
sentences.zh: 安东尼·福奇（Anthony Fauci）博士——

sentences.en: President Biden's chief medical advisor for COVID-19, said that most Americans could become eligible for the coronavirus vaccine as soon as April, but that administering it
sentences.zh: 作为拜登总统针对新冠肺炎疫情的首席医疗顾问，他表示绝大多数美国人最早可能在四月份就有资格接种新冠疫苗，但要将其分发下去

sentences.en: could take several months.
sentences.zh: 可能需要几个月的时间。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由

sentences.en: Astha Chathurvedi,
sentences.zh: 阿斯哈·查图维迪（Astha Chathurvedi）、

sentences.en: Rochelle Banja, and Rachel Quester.
sentences.zh: 罗谢尔·班加（Rochelle Banja）和雷切尔·奎斯特（Rachel Quester）制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by Lisa Chow and engineered by Chris Wood.
sentences.zh: 本期节目由丽莎·乔（Lisa Chow）剪辑，克里斯·伍德（Chris Wood）负责音频工程。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是本期《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.zh: 节假日过后的周二再见。

sentences.en: This week on The Wirecutter Show, we're getting ready for hosting over the holidays.
sentences.zh: 本周的《Wirecutter秀》将为您盘点如何为假期的聚会做好准备。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 收听节目，获取让客人们宾至如归的小贴士。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们对光线极度敏感、需要漆黑环境才能入睡吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean, do they blackout to go to sleep?
sentences.zh: 我指的不是他们是不是喝到断片才能睡着。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们对光线有什么要求？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为这真的是一个非常具体的问题。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies?
sentences.zh: 他们有什么过敏症吗？

sentences.en: Food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 饮食敏感吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们习惯喝咖啡还是喝茶？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？

sentences.zh: 请在《纽约时报》应用程序上或您喜欢的任何地方收听《Wirecutter秀》。
